'''A. K. M. Fazle Hussain''' ({{langx|bn|এ.কে.এম. ফজলে হুসাইন}}; born 20 January 1943, in [[Bangladesh]]) is a professor of [[mechanical engineering]] at [[Texas Tech University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.depts.ttu.edu/me/faculty/fazle_hussain/index.php|title=Fazle Hussain, Ph.D. {{!}} Faculty {{!}} Mechanical Engineering {{!}} TTU|website=www.depts.ttu.edu|access-date=2019-12-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fazle |first=Hussain |date=2019 |title=Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.depts.ttu.edu/me/faculty/fazle_hussain/FazleCVNov2019.pdf}}</ref>

==Education==
Hussain graduated with a BS in mechanical engineering from [[Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology]] in 1963.<ref name=":0" /> He went on to attend [[Stanford University]], where he studied under [[William Craig Reynolds]],{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}} and received his MS and PhD in mechanical engineering in 1966 and 1969.<ref name=":0" />; he was awarded in 1971 the best PhD dissertation award by Stanford. 

Afterwards, Hussain was a post-doctoral fellow at the [[Johns Hopkins University]] with [[Leslie S. G. Kovasznay]] and [[Stanley Corrsin]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}}

== Career ==
Hussain was a professor of mechanical engineering at [[University of Houston]] from 1976 to 2013. More recently, he was also a professor in the Earth & atmospheric science and physics departments from 2007 to 2013.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.me.uh.edu/faculty/hussain|title=Dr. Fazle Hussain|last=University of Houston|date=2015-09-18|website=UH Department of Mechanical Engineering|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-26}}</ref> At UH, he held the Cullen Professorship in mechanical engineering.<ref>{{cite news |title=1999 President's Report |url=https://www.uh.edu/learningleading/docs/PrezReport.pdf |publisher=University of Houston |date=1999}}</ref>

In 2001, Hussain was inducted into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for "fundamental experiments and concepts concerning important structures in turbulence, vortex dynamics, and acoustics, and for new turbulence measurement techniques."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/30187/Dr-Fazle-Hussain|title=Dr. Fazle Hussain|last=|first=|date=2001|website=NAE Website|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-12-04}}</ref> He is also a member of the advisory board at [[Shahjalal University of Science and Technology]].{{Citation needed|date=February 2020}}

==Honors and awards==
* Freeman Scholar Award of [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]] in 1984<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/literature-awards/freeman-scholar-award | title=Freeman Scholar Award}}</ref><ref name="scholarsbangladesh.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.scholarsbangladesh.com/fazle_hussain.php/|title=welcome to Scholarsbangladesh.com|work=scholarsbangladesh.com|access-date=1 October 2011|archive-date=7 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707175515/http://scholarsbangladesh.com/fazle_hussain.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Fluids Engineering Award of [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers|ASME]] in 2000<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/fluids-engineering-award |title = Fluids Engineering Award}}</ref>
* Fluid Dynamics Award of [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics|AIAA]] in 2002<ref name="scholarsbangladesh.com"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiaa.org/content.cfm?pageid=401&AwardView=Type&LUPARTICIPATIONCODE=HAFD|title=The American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics >> AWARDS DIRECTORY|last=|first=|date=|work=aiaa.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050424160935/http://www.aiaa.org/content.cfm?pageid=401|archive-date=2005-04-24|access-date=}}</ref>
* Fluid Dynamics Prize of the American Physical Society in 1998.
